lessons.title: Suspend functions versus threads
lessons.summary: If answer() is called directly from this ordinary main without runBlocking, what happens?
explanation: suspend is a Kotlin language modifier allowing a function to call suspending operations. It does not automatically start a thread, choose a dispatcher or make a blocking call nonblocking. This answer function returns immediately but must still be called from a suspending context.

lessons.title: Cooperative cancellation
lessons.summary: If the finally message changes to "released", which order is guaranteed?
explanation: A Job cancellation is a request, not a forced thread kill. Suspending library functions check cancellation; CPU-bound work must also cooperate. ensureActive is an optional reference for a later CPU-loop design, not an additional call required in this suspending handshake example. Do not swallow CancellationException as an ordinary successful result.

CompletableDeferred<Unit> is a one-shot completion signal: complete(Unit) releases await without carrying useful data. The child then waits in awaitCancellation, which suspends until cancelled and never returns normally. cancelAndJoin requests cancellation and waits for cleanup. finally runs during this exit; it must not start suspending cleanup without an appropriate explicit policy.

lessons.title: Java platform types and null boundaries
lessons.summary: If the property is set to "read" before retrieval, what prints?
explanation: A Java method without sufficiently specific nullability information can appear as a platform type, often displayed as String! in tooling. The exclamation form is not Kotlin source syntax. Assigning such a result to a non-null Kotlin type can fail at runtime if Java returns null.

System.getProperty can return null when a property is absent. This isolated JVM fixture first clears its uniquely named property, then assigns the result to String?. The safe call plus Elvis operator handles absence without !!. These changes affect only this short-lived process, not an operating-system environment variable.

Complete local Kotlin/JVM example; the app itself does not execute it:
```kotlin


fun main() {
    val key = "codequest.lesson.optional.topic"
    System.clearProperty(key)
    val topic: String? = System.getProperty(key)
    println(topic?.length ?: -1)
}
```
Expected output or behavior: -1. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Explain the difference between choosing String? at a boundary and forcing an uncertain value with !!. You may trace it without a Kotlin compiler; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
